#3979. Holiday Gaming With Kids And Family

Ahead of the holiday season, we gathered some of our favorite video game recommendations focused on family interaction, spoke with Jackbox Games and Halfbrick (creators of Bluey’s Quest for the Gold Pen) about what it takes to make a game that everyone can enjoy together, and even have tips for new parent gamers hoping to introduce kids to their (and our) favorite hobby.

From its inception, video games were created to encourage social interaction. Tennis for Two in 1958, arguably the first video game, had two players compete in digital tennis against one another. The single-player video game came later, and as much as we love them, some of our best gaming memories are centered around playing with family and friends. And as we get older, we’re making new gaming memories with our own kids.

Making video games is hard. That any game crosses the finish line is a miracle of teamwork and perseverance, and the hardest trick of all is making the final product feel effortless. Arguably, none are more practiced at feeling like effortless joy machines than the games that effectively include players of all ages and skill levels in the experience. And to take it a step further, Jackbox Games is perhaps the best at this sub-genre of video games: inclusive party games that are genuinely for everyone.

Jackbox Games studio creative director Arnie Niekamp sheepishly and humbly agrees when I offer this accolade and also says thank you. “It really matters to us,” Niekamp says. “We really value, first, just inclusivity in general, and are always trying to think of how we can make our games playable by as many people as possible, or how we can expand that.”

Jackbox Games has released its 12th Party Pack by the time you’re reading this issue, and part of the secret of that ongoing success is that its creators stick with the company for a long time. “The person that came in and started making games as a young single person also ages into having a family, having kids, and having that perspective of, ‘Oh wait, it’s also really fun to play these games with my kids, with my family.’”

Even if a game is primarily focused towards young players, being fun for everyone is “very important” Halfbrick writer Brendan Deboy says when talking about making Bluey’s Quest for the Gold Pen. “Bluey’s humor, relationships and themes give children and parents reasons to enjoy its stories together. We wanted that shared enjoyment to carry into the game.”

Brooke Breit, Jackbox’s game product manager and The Jackbox Party Pack 12’s lead, cites that family element as an important detail to making games for everyone. “We playtest our games constantly throughout production amongst ourselves, and that’s one of the markers of, ‘Are we hitting success within the mechanics? Within how it plays?’” Breit says. “And part of that also involves us playing with our own families as a part of that playtesting process [...] All of our kids have a lot of opinions on what makes a really good Jackbox game.”

Breit also points out a metric the team has accidentally discovered over the years that has helped them figure out why a game works for all ages when the creation process happens to be going well. “There’s a little bit of… maybe the younger and older crowd also intersects with the drunk crowd,” Breit says with a thoughtful laugh.

Deboy also discusses the importance of family playtesting saying, “Children of Halfbrick parents playtested the game, with ages ranging from four to 10. Their parents reported what they enjoyed most and where they became stuck.” And avoiding the stickiness is crucial. “We wanted challenges to be satisfying without any single obstacle preventing someone from seeing the rest of the game,” Deboy says. “If something is too difficult, they can leave it, try another activity and return later. Harder challenges were often tucked away in harder-to-find places, helping players encounter easier activities first.”

Jackbox also figured out another secret weapon for great family gaming and gaming with kids: getting away from cell phones. This may be an odd element to cite considering the vast majority of Jackbox games are played collectively on individual phones, but when you’re using your phone as a controller, you’re not using it to check social media.

“You can’t get phones out of people’s hands anyway, so you might as well use it as a tool,” Niekamp says. “Engagement is absolutely a huge part of our design, and we talk a lot about what is on your device,” Breit says. “What is on the game screen? Where do we want people’s focus to be at any given moment? And are we giving opportunity and motivation for people to talk to each other and actually engage with each other?”

Deboy cites another way to encourage engagement as it did with Halfbrick’s Bluey game. “We wanted everyone to be able to finish the game, while giving players of different ages and abilities things to enjoy. That meant providing choices. Some activities test timing and motor skills, while others reward exploration, searching or logical thinking. Players can choose what suits them without having to complete every obstacle.”

When asked what other cooperative and family-focused games are doing right and wrong, Deboy and the Halfbrick team recalled games they played (and got annoyed with) when they were young. “Some of us remembered childhood games where one difficult boss or tricky section stopped us from ever reaching the end,” Deboy says. “You could spend weekend after weekend trying, or replay the opening levels because those were the only ones you could finish. That experience informed our approach.”

Niekamp points out his appreciation for games like Mario Party (which he calls brilliant, but wishes it moved a little faster), but mainly says there just aren’t enough fun co-op family games. “I wish there were more,” Niekamp says. “Especially when your kids are younger, there’s a real sweet spot of like… it’s so great when you start playing stuff together, and finding those things is so incredible and awesome, and then you just start to feel like you run through them pretty fast, and you’re sort of looking for more.”

We agree with Niekamp, and alongside helpful tips for how to introduce young or new players to video games, you can also read on for some of our recommendations (including a different, but similarly fun Bluey video game) for recent games we think are particularly suited to playing with your family.

Whether it’s your friend’s kids, nephews and nieces, or your own children, many of us are eventually confronted with the challenge: How can I share my love of gaming with someone younger who is just getting into the hobby, and enjoy the experience with them? Here are some tried-and-true tips that have served us well.

Especially with the youngest set, gaming can start with opportunities to watch and contribute as you play. Choose low-complexity exploration games with some freeform choices about where to go, cozy games with building options, or age-appropriate narrative games. You handle the controls, but let your kid choose how to proceed. Talk to them about what you’re doing. Tell them more about the game and why you like it. Help them feel like the cool things that happen are the result of their choices.

It should perhaps go without saying, but once they have their hands on the controller, accept moving slowly as a rule. Encourage small wins like learning which button does what. Don’t criticize mistakes. Acknowledge that losing and failing, and then coming back to try again, is part of the fun. Choose games with simple control inputs, easy modes, and forgiving restarts on failures. If you want them to eventually be able to play at your level, be patient enough that they want to keep playing.

Once they’re ready to actively play together, it’s hard to go wrong with cooperative play. In particular, watch for titles that allow one cooperative partner to help the other out of a bind with revives, carries, or boosts. Celebrate together when you overcome a notable challenge, even if you did most of the work.

Start with short sessions, and follow their interests and focus level. Even if you’re in the middle of an exciting section of a game, take a break when you sense they’re getting frustrated – at least at first. Regardless, don’t play too long. Resilience in confronting really tough encounters, puzzles, or challenges can come with time. Watch for things that are scary – even if they don’t seem like they should be scary – and either divert from that thing, or talk together about the difference between a game and real life.

There are plenty of amazing online games, and many can be safe to play with kids. But other players add a level of randomness that can lead to major frustration, unsafe incoming communication, and wildly different skill levels. Start with games that don’t require playing with others online, and if you do graduate to online play at some point, stay directly involved in play sessions.

While you can introduce your favorites, kids will quickly learn what they like. Follow that enthusiasm, and engage with the games and experiences they’re excited about. Ignore the advice above that doesn’t apply to your new gamer; some kids will love competitive play or be eager to confront high challenge and frustration, and that’s just fine. Like most things about raising kids – listen to what they’re communicating, and build what they love into your gaming together.

Good family games have the potential to become memorable staples in bonding and communication. Here are some recent games we’d recommend for playing together with the people you love and the people who annoy you (but you still love them anyway).

Parents likely need no introduction to the Heeler family; the anthropomorphic dogs are nearly ubiquitous in popular culture. Thankfully, Bluey and friends’ newest video game is a welcome treat, offering stress-free, simple gameplay you can enjoy solo or with a partner. Bluey finds an old Polaroid-style camera and sets out to scrapbook, snapping pictures of all sorts of animals, games, and friends as she explores sites like the Park and Riverbank, often unlocking additional stickers and decorations for her new hobby. Like the show, Happy Snaps is charming and often funny, and its sandbox-style exploration hints at a refreshing curiosity about the world. - Matt Miller

Some games can be fun multiplayer experiences even if they weren’t intended to be. Solving dense puzzles in Blue Prince or Lorelai and the Laser Eyes as a group is fun, but if you’re mixing in younger players, grab The Mermaid Mask. Captain Magnus Mortuga was murdered aboard his submarine, and the killer is still loose; you’re tasked with gathering testimony, analyzing evidence, and solving bizarre puzzles. Charming animations and voice performances make this a great fit for family, so long as they’re old enough to handle cartoon bloodstains and themes of mortality. - Charles Harte

The loot-driven action of the Diablo franchise is a potent mix of multiplayer and RPG mechanics that just about any fan of video games can appreciate. But its violence and tone mean it’s not one you necessarily want to play with younger adventurers. Minecraft Dungeons and its recently released sequel, however, offer the same fun RPG growth trajectory and accessible combat without all that pesky blood. The game also offers local multiplayer for up to four players, which means it’s very easy for the family to get together and play in a world the kids are likely already very familiar with. - Kyle Hilliard

Released on Switch in 2023 and ported to Switch 2 with myriad added bells and whistles in 2026, Super Mario Bros. Wonder expertly toes the line between new and old. Fans of Mario’s NES roots can enjoy the plumber’s latest adventure and experience some of the best 2D platforming the medium offers, and new players get to learn what makes the world of Mario so charming. With multiple playable characters, local co-op play, and lots of options to try different abilities, Wonder is a great introduction to Mario and also just a great game. - Kyle Hilliard

Disney Illusion Island is an all-ages adventure that can double as your child’s first-ever platformer and a family co-op session centered around the joy of movement in games. Play as Disney’s iconic Fab Four – Mickey, Minnie, Donald, and Goofy – as you explore the various biomes of the mythical Monoth while trying to save its inhabitants. There’s no combat, so even your littlest ones can enjoy the fun of exploring these beautifully hand-drawn 2D spaces, and hilarious cutscenes will have everyone on the couch laughing. Three free DLCs will keep the adventure going after credits, too. - Wesley Leblanc

When it comes to playing a video game with family of any age – young, old, or in the middle – you really can’t go wrong with a Jackbox game. There is some reading required, but if you know how to use a phone, then you can participate, and you will enjoy yourself. 12 includes a game about sorting trivia questions into the right categories at high speed, one where you try to make the most ridiculous greeting card, a game encouraging silly debates, one that identifies connections among everyone playing, and finally Hyperface, where you manipulate selfies. Just make sure to toggle on the “family-friendly” option in the settings to omit some of the more adult jokes and prompts. - Kyle Hilliard

Everyone remembers the excitement of Wii Sports back in 2006. That game, with its fun selection of tech-demo sports minigames, permeated pop culture and reached a mainstream audience in ways few other games can claim. Nintendo Switch Sports Resort may not have the same cultural impact as Wii Sports, but it’s a superbly fun and approachable collection of sports-based minigames. Whether you want to reignite your love for virtual bowling and archery or cruise around Wuhu Island on land, sea, or air, Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is an enjoyable experience that’s simple to pick up and play for gamers of all ages and experience levels. Read our full review. - Brian Shea

Convincing kids to do a family activity isn’t always an easy task, but saying the words, “You can play as Spider-Man,” makes it a whole lot smoother. Marvel Cosmic Invasion is a beat ’em up reminiscent of arcade classics from the ’90s, but with modern controls and conveniences. Kids will have fun with favorites like Iron Man, Captain America, and Black Panther, while older superhero fans will appreciate inclusions like Phyla-Vell and Beta Ray Bill. With approachable controls, vibrant pixel art, and an electric soundtrack, it makes for a super Saturday morning experience. - Charles Harte

Since the world of Pokémon debuted in Japan in 1996 on the Game Boy, it has evolved to become a cross-generational staple for nostalgic adults and young players eager to learn about and pick their favorite creature. Pokopia is arguably the best Pokémon game in years and is a much more relaxing affair than the games that revolve around combat. Progress requires some reading, and it’s worth noting that the multiplayer options are limited, complicated, and require multiple Switch 2 consoles. But as a fun pass-the-controller way to work together and build a new world for all your Pokémon experience, it is an undeniable success. - Kyle Hilliard

Mario Party is admittedly the king of the board game-style genre it popularized (and 2024’s Super Mario Party Jamboree is a great option in that regard), but Lego Party is a genuine contender for the genre crown. The Lego of it all offers more flexibility in terms of theming for worlds and minigames. Players also vote on the minigames they want to play, and winning awards more than just currency – it also affects subsequent turn order, which makes it all feel a little more rewarding. The consistent commentary is also genuinely funny and helps keep everyone engaged while others take their turns. - Kyle Hilliard

There are some games that are just known to be great for families that, frankly, you probably don’t even need to be reminded of. There is a reason millions play Fortnite every day; Mario Kart, Mario Party, and Smash Bros. are among Nintendo’s best-selling games of all time, and it’s so easy to get lost in a Minecraft world of your own creation. These games are family staples, but just in case you weren’t already familiar, you should probably check them out.

#3978. Report: Major Details Revealed About Xbox's Original Plan For Project Helix

"Xbox Helix’s original plan was far more radical than we knew"

We've been hearing about Xbox's Project Helix console for some time now, with Xbox always talking very vaguely about what we can expect from it, and perhaps that's because the vision has changed for the system over the years.

Today, the folks over at Windows Central are revealing details about the "original plan" for Xbox Project Helix, which include that it was going to be a "full gaming PC" akin to the ROG Xbox Ally with the ability to run console games on top. Steam support would have been included, as would have Windows 11 in general.

They were seemingly even going to drop the paywall for multiplayer games in the process.

"The original plan for Helix, which ran under a different codename until last summer, was for it to essentially be a full gaming PC with the capability to run all of your existing Xbox console games on top. It would be functionally similar to the Xbox Ally PC gaming handheld, with a gamepad-first Xbox-style full-screen interface, complete with the capability to exit out to the Windows desktop and install whatever you want. That, indeed, included Steam.

As part of this strategy, Xbox would have had no choice but to drop the paywall for multiplayer from Xbox Game Pass (formerly Xbox Live Gold). There's no universe where a true PC could function with a multiplayer paywall. I understand that, indeed, removing the paywall was costed into this strategy."

All of this was apparently conceived prior to the component crisis that's caused hardware prices to rise significantly in recent times, and ultimately there's a feeling that the plan might have changed somewhat as a result.

Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has also become the head of the brand since Helix was in the conception phase, and she may have her own ideas about dropping multiplayer paywalls and integrating Steam into the next-gen console. After all, a lot of people have wondered what Xbox stands to gain by partnering with Steam instead of focusing on the Xbox Store.

It's important to highlight here that nobody knows what the current plan is at Xbox HQ, and Windows Central theorises that "maybe Microsoft doesn't even know itself". There's every chance we still may be looking at a console that can run Steam games and not require a multiplayer paywall, but there's probably an equal chance that Xbox has gone back the drawing board and decided to reel in its scope when it comes to PC support.

Let's wait and see, eh? We know we're definitely getting the ability to play PC titles on Xbox Project Helix no matter what, but the safe bet is that it'll be via the Xbox Store - and who knows what'll happen with the multiplayer side of things.

For what it's worth, Xbox has this month committed to Helix being a console and not a PC, which seemingly goes against the original plan for a so-called "full gaming PC". In that regard, it appears that things have changed.

"We're very clear on the design goal: Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC. It is not a PC that can also play console games. The goal is making it easy, intuitive, and instant to access my games. But if you're a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customizability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it."

News 'The Ultimate Gaming Machine' - Xbox Reveals Tons Of New Project Helix Information

Also clarifying that it's definitely a console and not a PC

News Xbox CTO Issues Statement On How Project Helix OS Is Being 'Built On Windows'

Which perhaps confusingly means it'll likely follow the Series X and S

I will never see a GOG, Epic or Steam launcher on the console.

I have said time and time and time again that it makes no sense whatsoever for Microsoft to release a console that is essentially a PC that provides access to the likes of Steam. None whatsoever! And of course, I have had an enormous amount of pushback from some people on these forums.

I have said time and time again that people would simply switch to buying their games on Steam because they are cheaper there. Even now, a quick look on Loaded at Steam at games that are coming out on Steam and Xbox shows:

*Stranger Than Heaven Deluxe Edition £79.99 on the Xbox Store, and £64.99 for Steam. A saving of £15. *Persona 4 Revival Premium Edition £84.99 on the Xbox Store, and £69.99 for Steam. A saving of £15. *Metro 2039 Standard Edition £59.99 on the Xbox Store, and £40.49 for Steam. A saving of £19.50. *Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World Digital Deluxe Edition, which is £79.99 on the Xbox Store and £61.49 for Steam. A saving of £18.50.

These are not guesses on my part. They can be looked up right now. So if you were interested in buying each of these 4 games, you would save £68.00 by buying them for Steam, which means you would have saved enough to buy a fifth game. So why would you buy these games on Xbox? And let's not forget, when Steam has a sale, they undercut the Xbox Store then too meaning you can save even more still.

Again, I have said before that if Helix offers PC game play, then they have to drop the online paywall. Even if Helix only offers access to the Microsoft Store, then they will have to drop the online paywall because that is already the case for those that currently buy games through the Microsoft Store, and it is why PC Games Pass is cheaper as it takes into account that there is no online paywall on PC.

Problem is, most of us that have Essential only do so because it is, well... essential to have if you want to play online. Get rid of the online paywall and many of us will no longer need Essential, so a whole swathe of people will suddenly abandon Game Pass. And I'd wager there are a lot of people that would leave Premium and Ultimate too. Right now some will only have those tiers because they are better than Essential, but they really only want online access. Make that free, and then the imperative of having Games Pass is gone, and if they don't feel they are getting value from the service, then they too can quit without losing access to online play.

I know a lot of people really want Helix to be a PC that offers access to Steam, but honestly, they really need to be careful about what they wish for, because as I have said many times now, Steam would be the downfall of Xbox because once people see what savings they can make on Steam Microsoft will lose billions in revenue...

One last thing, as I have said before, if Helix offers PC gaming including access to Steam, then I do not think Microsoft will be able to subsidise it at all. The reason is fairly simple; if Helix is seen as a decent entry point PC, and it is subsidised making it significantly cheaper than it would be to build a similar PC yourself, then people will buy it to use as a Steam machine. They will completely sidestep the Xbox Store. That would mean that not only would Microsoft be selling Helix at a loss, but also they would not make a penny from those that bought it. The only reason the likes of Microsoft and Sony subsidise consoles right now is because they make back the losses on the price of the console through sales on their Stores. So, if Helix is essentially a PC Microsoft will sell it either for the cost of making it, or with a slight profit.

Sony, on the other hand, can subsidise the PS6 because they will be locking their customers into buying games through the PlayStation Store.

So, if Helix were to cost £1000 to make, then the least that Microsoft would sell it for would be £1000. If the PS6 costs the same to make, then Sony could subsidise it and see it cost £900 or even £800.

Thing is, if Helix really is a PC capable device, then it is likely to cost much more than £1000 meaning the gap in between Helix and the PS6 could be far greater than £200.

So if the PS6 is sold for £800 (and I think that is what Sony will aim for), and Helix is sold for £1200 (and I think it could be more than that as PC components are not cheap) then that is a difference of £400, and that difference maybe enough to persuade a not insignificant number of people to switch from Xbox to PlayStation.

Obviously, I have no idea what Helix will be. I have no idea of how much either Helix or the PS6 will be sold at. I just know that enabling us to purchase games through and for Steam on Helix will be absolutely disastrous for Xbox, and so I really hope they have the sense to change course and not give us access to it as I want to be gaming on an Xbox for many generations yet...

#3977. "We Saw Your Hopeful Requests" - Fabraz Announces Demon Tides Switch 2 Release

Launching January 2027 alongside the Switch version

Critically-acclaimed developer Fabraz has announced it will be releasing its 3D platformer Demon Tides for the Switch on 21st January 2027.

As part of this news, it's also been revealed Demon Tides is launching for the Switch 2 (and PlayStation 5) on the same date! These versions of the game are done in partnership with PM Studios and will get the physical treatment at some point "later" next year.

"Demon Tides will launch on the Switch, Switch 2 and PS5 on January 21st 2027! Demon Tides had a critically acclaimed PC launch with a 95% Overwhelmingly Positive rating on Steam, 84 on metacritic and 86 on opencritic."

Fangamer's physical version of Demon Turf + Demon Tides will also be going into production "soon", with pre-orders for this scheduled to go live in early 2027. This version will also come bundled with Neon Splash.

Fabraz has also confirmed the Switch 1 version of the game will feature an option to uncap the frame rate, meaning you play the Switch 1 version in 60fps on Switch 2.

As for how each version of the game performs on its respective system, you can expect 30fps at 720p/1080p (docked and handheld) on Switch. And on Switch 2, the game runs at 60fps in performance mode, 30fps in quality mode, and displays at a 1080p resolution.

In some other news, Fabraz recently rolled out a patch for Atari's revival of Bubsy, bumping his 4D outing up to Version 1.2.1.

#3976. GTA 6 Fashion Is Taking Social Media by Storm

GTA 6 is not only taking the gaming world by storm – it’s also taking the fashion world by storm, it seems.

While you don’t get to create your own character in Rockstar’s latest release, you can style protagonists Jason and Lucia however you like.

And while I had fun with this aspect during the review period, I’m flabbergasted by the creations people are coming up with.

I think what’s really interesting is how every individual Jason and Lucia is becoming a reflection of each player’s personality.

You can see the contrast in the two styles below.

One couple looks like they’re about to attend a music festival while the other looks like they’re about to go to an art gallery:

And then you have this version which looks like it’s stepped straight off the set of an expensive fragrance commercial:

The game is so malleable, with such a range of expression, that you can kinda present the characters however you like.

But this one looks like a 00s pop punk singer:

And it’s not just the makeup and hairstyles either – it’s the full range. Look at these ensembles put together by one user:

Pair all of that with one of the best photo modes ever included in a game, allowing you to place dynamic studio lighting, and you have a surprising outlet for creativity:

Never, in my wildest dreams, did I imagine I’d be writing an article like this about a GTA game. But it’s just a testament to the groundbreaking experience Rockstar has delivered.

How are you styling your Jason and Lucia? Show off your fashion skills in the comments section below.

#3975. Never one to lag behind HSR and ZZZ, Genshin Impact will introduce its own new pink-haired animal-themed girl in Version Luna 6

Plus Mondstadt is expanding yet further north in Genshin Impact's Luna 6 update.

Today’s Genshin Impact Special Program has wrapped up, and it’s brought us some big news about the next major update. Luna 6 is the next phase in the action RPG’s story, titled Song of the Welkin Moon: Rondo - Augured Homecoming.

It’s set to arrive on April 8, bringing with it a tonne of new content, including a big expansion to the original region of Mondstadt.

As part of this new update, Mondstadt’s northern parts expand with new areas. The new Dornman Port is one thing, but the most exciting is the Temple of Space. This floating structure is home to Asmoday fragments, and is made up of different realms inspired by Liyue, Sumeru, and various other civilizations from around Teyvat. Launching with the update is a new mechanic that lets you manipulate the space to reveal hidden paths containing secrets.

If you take the time to explore, you’ll find a lot to there to learn about Asmoday, Ruler of Space. There’s a new boss to take on in the temple, too: Watcher: Fallen Vigil.

The only new character in Luna 6 is Linnea, who continues the current trend within HoYoverse games of focussing heavily on cute pink-haired animal-themed girls. Linnea is a 5-Star Geo Bow user who can really work with parties made up of Lunar-Crystallize characters, with her big gimmick being the ability to turn Hydro-Crystallize reactions into Lunar-Crystallize reactions.

Linnea has a companion, Lumi, who allows her to increase the Lunar-Crystallize damage she deals, while also lowering her enemies’ Geo resistance. Linnea can also deliver either off-field Geo damage or a Lunar-Crystallize reaction hit with her Elemental Skill.

Beyond that, she can heal the party using her Elemental Burst. If you take Linnea with you as you explore, she can help you discover rare animals, thanks to her innate naturalist abilities.

This update will also see Chasca get her first-ever rerun, and you’ll be able to roll for her in the first phase of Event Wishes. The second phase will feature no new characters and instead focus on Nefer and Lauma. There’s going to be another Chronicled Wish banner, this time specifically for Fontaine characters.

You can look forward to a few other new arrivals in Luna 6, including The Nod-Krai Trade Expo, some quality of life updates to Miliastra Wonderland to up the number of players in each lobby, not to mention various other UI changes.

Catch up on the latest Genshin Impact codes before you jump for some freebies.

#3974. Pokémon Champions Is Adding Four More Mega Evolutions In A New Update Next Week

24 newly added Pokémon will also be available for battle

Following the news of a Pokémon Champions balance patch update, The Pokémon Company has now revealed some new competitors are preparing to arrive in the free-to-play battle title.

On 2nd December 2026, Regulation Set M-D will see the arrival of Mega Heatran and Mega Tatsugiri. All up, there will be 24 newly added Pokémon available for battle and four more Mega Evolutions.

Here's the full announcement from the official Pokémon website:

Some new competitors are preparing for battle! Regulation Set M-D will run in Pokémon Champions from Wednesday, December 2, 2026, at 6:00 p.m. PST to Wednesday, March 3, 2027, at 5:59 p.m. PST. Pokémon that were eligible for Ranked Battles in previous regulation sets remain eligible, but they’ll be joined by Heatran, Dondozo, Tatsugiri, and more!

Even more Mega Evolutions are gearing up for a fight under Regulation Set M-D, including Mega Heatran and Mega Tatsugiri. Following the update, there will be a total of 24 newly added Pokémon available for battle, along with four Mega Evolutions.

You can see the full roster in your game by following these steps:

- Go to Recruit. - Select Recruit Pokémon. - Select Roster Info.

Best of luck with your battles in Pokémon Champions, Trainers!

Here's some more information about what you can expect from Mega Heatran and Mega Tatsugiri (via Serebii.net):

- Mega Heatran has Water Compaction, which boosts its Defense by 2 Stages when hit by a Water-type Move - Mega Tatsugiri has a new Ability which increases its Special Attack by 1 stage when it enters battle

Again, this will arrive alongside a balance update on the same date. You can find out more about this in last week's post.

#3973. GTA 6 Vintage Vice City Pack Now Available To All Players On Xbox, And It's Pretty Cheap

"Flash back to when the neon burned brightest"

Ahead of the release of GTA 6, there were three types of content made available for it - the standard game, the Ultimate Edition content, and the Vintage Vice City Pack. The latter was intended as a pre-order bonus across Xbox and PS5.

Now that the game is out in the wild though, Rockstar Games has decided to make the Vintage Vice City Pack available to purchase on the Xbox Store, carrying a price tag of £4.49 / $4.99. That's obviously not as good as getting it for free, but it's pretty cheap all the same, and a nice option to have if you missed out on the pre-order period.

Similar to the Ultimate Edition content that you can also buy separately for £20.00 / $20.00, these items are made available "as [the] story progresses", so you don't necessarily get it all at the beginning of the campaign.

I have to admit that I haven't really engaged with the Ultimate Edition stuff all that much yet, although it's certainly a nice bonus to get extra vehicles, liveries and outfits. The game is more than stacked enough that you don't need to buy anything more than the standard edition, but the option is there if you want the most content possible.

We'll leave a poll down below to find out which version you personally have, and let us know in the comments if you think the Vintage Vice City Pack and/or the Ultimate Edition content is worth buying on top of GTA 6 itself!

#3972. Caleb's third Myth has finally arrived in Love and Deepspace, and it's good news for all the husbandbro fans out there

Love and Deepspace has kicked off a new event, squarely built around Caleb's new Memory Pair.

Love and Deepspace’s latest update is here, adding a new Memory Pair for Caleb. The event is dubbed Ghosts' Final March, and it’s available now as part of a new Limited Wish Pool, as it has always worked.

The new Memory Pair is a 5-Star Solar-Slot, which can be obtained through the aforementioned Wish Pool. Doing so will unlock the Netherlord Companion for Caleb, and there’s even more for you to explore in this one.

Alongside the big new Memory Pair, Ghosts' Final March also offers the opportunity to earn a new 4-Star Solar-Slot Memory Pair, alongside ten Deepspace Wishes, 500 Diamonds, and other freebies. The event ends on April 11, so you have some time to get in and play.

If you’re only interested in the 5-Star variants, you’ll be happy to know that Infold is sticking with 150 pulls as the absolute maximum to guarantee earning Netherlord. This will be automatically unlocked after you pull both Nether Yearning and Nether Parting through the Wish Pool.

Obtaining either of the two will give you access to all chapters for the new Myth that’s also available as part of this event: Yin Yang Sundering. You can read all the lore once either of the two Memories have been unlocked, and you won’t even need to upgrade either of them.

The Lost Souls event has also kicked off alongside the new update. You can take part to claim a 4-Star Solar Slor Memory Pair for Caleb: Duskshard Dreams and Duskshard Lotus. You can also earn the 3-Star Memory, Lotus Bond, alongside some other freebies like more Wishes, Diamonds, Photo Poses, and an event-exclusive title.

After you unlock Caleb’s Netherlord Companion, you may want to fight alongside him to get another 4-Star Memory for free. You’ll need to challenge the the Rehearsal Stage to do so, and your first clear is guaranteed to get you the Duskshard Lotus Memory.

If you’re new to Love and Deepspace, or you simply want a refresher, we’ve put together a guide to help you wrap your head around Myths; how they work and how to unlock them. Banners are also an important part of any gacha game, Love and Deepspace included, so here’s how banners work, and what the current and next banners are.

And, as ever, it’s worth checking if you’re missing any of these Love and Deepspace codes to get some in-game freebies.

#3970. The Petit Planet beta is coming back with new updates, but you still need to hope for an invite

If you've been missing Petit Planet since it was last available to play, you'll be happy to know that HoYoverse is hosting another test soon.

It’s been quite a while since we’ve heard anything about Petit Planet, the upcoming game from Genshin Impact and Honkai: Star Rail developer HoYoverse. By most accounts, Petit Planet is the studio’s take on Animal Crossing, though with a few interesting ideas of its own.

The game’s most recent test took place all the way back in November, but its next big test isn’t far off.

HoYoverse announced today that Petit Planet’s Stardrift Test is scheduled for April 21. This latest build will be available on PC, Android, and iOS. The beta will include new Neighbors, an updated Starsea Voyage, and more for you to do at the Galactic Bazaar.

Seeing as interacting with Neighbors is a core part of this life sim RPG, the confirmation that new faces will be available in this test is big news. Each Neighbor in Petit Planet is a character, with their own personalty and life story.

The Starsea Voyage now includes a map, too, which you can use to take you to other Islets. If you played any of the previous tests, you should already be familiar with this feature.

The only bit of bad news here is that this remains a closed beta. You’re still encouraged to sign up on the official website, but you’re not guaranteed access. HoYoverse said that only a portion of players who sign up will be invited to the upcoming beta.

Petit Planet remains without a release date. If nothing else, it’ll be interesting to see the progress the game has made since last November’s beta.

#3969. Heartopia celebrates 30 million downloads with new outfits, permanent price cuts

Heartopia's rise has continued since its launch earlier this year, and the game's developer isn't slowing down with updates.

Heartopia has kicked off a new event to celebrate passing 30 million downloads. Just a couple of weeks after delivering the vintage Hollywood-themed Dreamlight Cinematics event, developer XD Games has revealed The Whimsical Tea Party, a limited-time Gilded Acorn Exhibition.

The event kicked off on Saturday, bringing some new themed content to the game.

Whimsical Tea Party’s biggest addition are the new outfits, including the Wandering Traveler, and the Duke Bunny outfits. Each outfit is available in three different colours. Another thing Heartopia events bring are building materials sets.

This one adds the Labyrinth furniture building materials set, the Hedgehog & Flamingo mallet, and the Cheshire Cat pet costume. Speaking of outfits, XD Games is dropping the in-game prices for a number of items permanently.

All original pet outfits now cost 66.7% less. Those of the Common variety will now cost 10 Souvenir Ticket Stubs, instead of the previous 30. Rare pet outfits will cost 5 Souvenir Ticket Stubs, down from 15.

If you happened to buy Common or Rare original pet outfits between July 17, 2024 and March 22, 2026, you’ll be refunded the difference. This will automatically show up in-game the next time you log in. If you instead purchased those pet outfits between March 23 and April 4, you should look forward to your refund before April 10.

Keeping with the theme of freebies, Heartopia is also celebrating surpassing 30 million downloads worldwide by giving all players a small gift package in-game. This freebie is available until May 29, so you should have enough time to claim it.

For comprehensive guidance on where to find birds, bugs, and fish, check out our Heartopia bird locations, Heartopia bug locations, and Heartopia fish locations guides. If you’re instead looking to find some wild vegetables for those cooking recipes, hit those links. And, as ever, it doesn’t hurt to see if you missed out on any Heartopia codes.

#3968. The Witch Life-Sim Witchbrook Has Officially "Gone Gold"

During the Indie World Showcase in October, it was confirmed the witch-themed life-sim and social RPG Witchbrook would be coming to the Switch 1 & 2 on 28th January 2027.

In an update from the developer this week, the team has now reassured Nintendo fans it's locked in for this date, as the game has officially "gone gold" on all platforms. Here's the message, along with a fitting in-game screenshot:

"We're delighted to announce that Witchbrook has GONE GOLD ALL PLATFORMS! We're can't wait for you all to join us on the journey on Jan 28th!"

Again, this basically means everything is currently on schedule, and the master copy is ready to go. Of course, "going gold" in the digital age means teams can still spend time polishing their title before the launch.

In this particular case, Witchbrook is getting an eShop release (with a physical version to follow), and we can probably expect some patches and updates as well. It was recently confirmed Witchbrook would also support crossplay between Switch 1 & 2 on release.

#3967. Digital Foundry Analyses Whether GTA 6 Could Benefit From 40FPS On Xbox Series X

"A 40fps mode with VRR could still make sense"

Over the weekend, there was a whole lot of buzz amongst the GTA 6 community about a Quick Resume glitch that unlocks the game's frame rate on Xbox Series X and S, potentially allowing it to reach 60FPS and higher.

Follow-up tests showed that the results were averaging more around the 30-35FPS range consistently, and some of the game's animations appeared to be running at double speed. The experts at Digital Foundry have now weighed in on this, and they've come to pretty much the same conclusion - that it's not really a viable way to play.

Rich Leadbetter of DF found that he reached an average of 36FPS on Xbox Series X in the first hour of the game:

"Unfortunately, while the unlock glitch is academically interesting, it doesn't provide a huge improvement to responsiveness. Our capture tools show frame-rates in the 30fps to 40fps range on Series X, with Rich recording an average frame-rate of 36fps during the first hour of the game."

The sped-up gameplay is also mentioned, described as an "oddity" that "makes the game inconsistent and harder to control", although this is said to be more likely a result of the bug rather than GTA 6's code being tied to frame rate.

Nevertheless, there's one specific advantage that's brought up as part of this glitch, which is that it reduces the game's input lag. Digital Foundry's tests showed that the game provided around 170ms of lag at the 30FPS mark, while a 40FPS scene dropped it to around 120ms. However, the varied frame rates are said to provide an "unsettling" feel overall, and one that probably outweighs the smoother feel during specific 30FPS+ moments.

The outlet says that a 40FPS mode when using a VRR supported display "could still make sense" on Xbox Series X, but "the game's CPU limits remain the largest barrier against such a mode" due to occasions where GTA 6 can't even reach 30FPS as things stand, while it might also require extra work such as implementing FSR upscaling tech.

"A 40fps mode with VRR could still make sense, but it's far from an open-and-shut case to say that such a mode would be an improvement overall against the current 30fps cap. It might also require extra work, such as integrated FSR 4 on Series X in service of a higher frame-rate when GPU limited, which wouldn't be the work of a moment. Finally, it looks like a 60fps mode is fundamentally unachievable on current console hardware."

Who knows whether Rockstar Games will be able to put in the work to provide a 40FPS mode in the future, but we're going to bet they'll stick with 30FPS and simply aim for 60FPS when Xbox Project Helix and the PS6 hit the market. They've got plenty of work to do with the PC version of GTA 6, not to mention the GTA Online version of the game that's surely in the works, so pushing to hit 40FPS on current-gen consoles seems unlikely.

Feature GTA 6's Unlocked Frame-Rate Glitch Tested: Is There a Case for 40fps?

Digital FoundryOur findings on Xbox Series X and Series S.

@AccessibleDaydream If the bottleneck is the GPU, then yes, but if it's the CPU, I'm afraid it won't improve performance.

@AccessibleDaydream FSR 4 intentionally lowers the rendering resolution and then uses AI to reconstruct the image. This is less demanding for the GPU than rendering directly at the native resolution because there are fewer pixels to process. As a result, the GPU saves rendering time and can use those saved resources to generate more frames per second (FPS). The end result is higher FPS with the same image quality, or in some cases even slightly better image quality

It's surprising that FSR 4.1 has not yet been introduced on Xbox Series X. The current Xbox Series X version already looks fantastic and is reportedly even better than the base PS5 version according to Digital Foundry's analysis.

@AccessibleDaydream Possibly, but probably not. Firstly as the unlocked framerate trick shows the game is mostly 30-35fps in most areas on Series X. Slightly higher in less busy areas, but still drops below 30fps on occasion. That means there isn't enough headroom to get to 40fps consistently.

As @Gabrie suggested the game seems like it is more constrained by the power of the CPU not the GPU. You can scale GPU tasks quite easily, but it's much harder to scale CPU tasks as it would basically mean lowering the complexity of the simulation (Cars, NPCs etc.) which they are unlikely to do.

On top of that FSR 4 is seemingly more computationally expensive than Rockstar's own upscaling solution. Therefore using FSR 4 would likely slow the game down, not speed it up. They could potentially run at lower base resolutions to speed it up again, and hope the upscaler gave a better, or passable, final image resolve, however if they were going to do that they likely would have done this when they put FSR 4 on the Series S version. It seems less likely now.

There is still a chance they manage to further optimise their code and find enough computational headroom to get to 40fps, but I think it's unlikely. That all said, while I am usually a bit of a frame rate snob the 30fps actually works fine in this game imo, it's very well implemented and feels smoother than it is.

@AccessibleDaydream FSR 4.1.2 is supported by over 400 PC games. It's a huge leap forward in terms of clarity, and it's also hyper-efficient as it fully uses RDNA2 native hardware instructions unlike post-process upscalers and PS5's QSSR. It would benefit the Series X version significantly if support is delivered via patch, and considering the fact that Series X already outperforms the PS5 version, it would be absolutely beneficial, even more considering that Series X has better VRR support than PS5.

Like others have said, probably they didn't want to add support on day one because of Sony's misleading (and paid) marketing claiming that it plays best on PS5, but the game code already includes FSR4 libraries ready for future support. That or that FSR4 released just weeks ago on Xbox. The latter is the reason considered in this DF's video.

As far as I know, GTA VI is the only game that supports FSR4 [on Series S.] They probably were using a temporal upscaler [on Series S], maybe something like FSR3, and they jumped at FSR4 and said, let's do this already because the alternative is clearly worse and we're already in the path of temporal upscaling for that console [Series S].

#3966. Honkai: Star Rail players are eating good, with Version 4.2 and third anniversary celebrations kicking off later this month

Honkai: Star Rail will be celebrating its third anniversary just days after it delivers a major update, and there's quite a bit to chew on in this one.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a stacked Honkai: Star Rail Special Program, delivering the one-two punch of revealing the game’s next major update, and detailing what you can expect from its third anniversary celebrations.

First off, Version 4.2, dubbed So Laughed the Masses, arrives April 22, making two characters playable, and bringing back a host of beloved characters for re-runs. The new update continues the Phantasmoon Games arc, as the story takes an especially suspect new development.

The big inciting incident of this new chapter is the reveal that whoever wins the Phantasmoon Games will also become the permanent Aeon of Elation. Meanwhile, Fulwish has invited all Supplicants to the Fulwish TV HQ to announce their intention to host a TV debate about the ultimate goal of the Phantasmoon Games.

Naturally, you’re invited, and you’ll have to overcome the challenges that await to gather more Wishpower.

Our first new arrival is Silver Wolf LV.999, with whom you should already be familiar from her Version 1 form. The difference now, of course, is that she’s getting a brand-new alternate kit, since — true to her new name — she's evolved into a Godmode Player upon reaching Level 999. Silver Wolf LV.999 is a 5-Star Imaginary character on the Path of Elation.

Her main combat trick is the ability to rack up Hidden MMR, which is what allows her to eventually activate her Cartridge and settle into the aforementioned Godmode state. While in that form, she shifts the entire battle into the virtual world, pulling in both teams into her gaming domain.

This is essentially a world under her control, which is why she can unlock a Reward Stage at the start of her turn, which lets her spawn in-game items. When picked up, these items can turn the tide of battle.

Keeping up with the ultra-gamer persona, Silver Wolf's Aha Instant strike blasts all enemies with a laser cannon, dealing massive damage. Perhaps her most interesting ability is being able to hack into the battlefield when she’s not actively on the team, something she can do when a teammate falls under enemy control.

Evanescia is the other newly-playable character, who has thus far only been an observer of the Phantasmoon Games, as well as one of the most prominent new characters we've met so far on Planarcadia. V4.2 sees the girl join the roster as a 5-Star Physical character who’s likewise on the Path of Elation. As she fights, she always accumulates Certified Banger, when she earns the title she’s able to simultaneously regenerate Energy and maintain her damage.

Evanescia’s damage continues to increase the more Certified Banger she accumulates, triggering an attack from Master Fox upon reaching a certain threshold, which deals damage to all enemies and regenerates Energy for herself. Her Elation Skill adds a bit of a performance to her kit, and is capable of hitting all enemies.

You may have noticed the Path of Elation theme in this one, so you won’t be surprised to learn that the Elation Trailblazer variant on the main playable character is also joining the team in 4.2. There’s a new weapon that starts off as a glow stick but can transform into a lightblade as you deal damage, and, yes, gain Certified Banger.

It can also turn into nunchucks, which delivers a unique flurry of attacks on all enemies surrounding the character, dealing multiple instances of damage. You can also use it to cheer for a teammate, hyping them up.

Version 4.2 Warp Events will bring back six characters. The first half will see reruns of The Dahlia, Castorice, and Firefly. The second half will give you another shot at unlocking Tribbie, Sunday, and Feixiao. What’s more, four of the game’s characters will be buffed in this update, so you may want to reconsider putting them them back on your team. They are Firefly, Huohuo, Seele, and Welt.

As part of the same update, you can expect the debut of the Cosmic Data Roaming event, which goes live alongside the anniversary celebrations. The event lets you live the life of a streamer.

Currency Wars is getting a big expansion, too. Likewise, the Cosmicon Collective is getting its version 2.0 update, adding new decks, dice as well as a new team challenge game mode.

As for the big third anniversary celebration, it will kick off in-game on April 26, bringing back Festive Gifts. The event will only be available during these celebrations, and it will once again be gifting players who log in regularly a total of 20 pulls.

You’ll also be able to a select a blessing card from a companion of your choice to receive a special gift of 1,600 Stellar Jades. The same celebrations will also seeHuohuo and Robin permanently added to the Stellar Convergence store. You’ll have another chance to exchange a Golden Companion Spirit for any companion you like in that store, too — and all you need to do is log in anytime between Versions 4.2 and 4.4. This being a new year for Honkai: Star Rail, the top-up double bonus is resetting, meaning anyone who tops up their wallet will get a hefty bonus.

Elsewhere, you’ll find new items in the Gift of Stardust Store, including a new outfit for Castorice. Between the time 4.2 launches and when the celebrations begin, you’ll be able to try your luck in Aha's Chosen: Spreading Elation Everywhere, an online event where you can leave a message for a chance to win various prizes.

#3964. Animal Crossing: New Horizons gets a new item to celebrate 25 years of the series

The allegedly finished game might finally, truly be feature complete with the addition of an anniversary item.

Animal Crossing: New Horizons has received a surprise patch today to celebrate the 25th anniversary of the life sim series. The update, version 3.0.2, is available across the Switch and Switch 2 versions of the game.

The patch brings a single new addition to New Horizons - a leaf item. Everyone gets it, too, so you don’t have to do anything special to acquire it.

After installing the patch, simply head to your in-house mailbox to claim it. The mail includes a hearty message to fans who supported the series for years, featuring an appropriate Nintendo N64 stamp.

The Leaf Statue, as it’s referred to in-game, lights up when placed.

April 14, 2011 marks the release of the original, lesser-known version of Animal Crossing in Japan. The game was initially released as Animal Forest (Dobutsu no Mori) on the Nintendo N64, before later making its way to the Nintendo GameCube in December of the same year as Dobutsu no Mori+ with some extra features.

That same, original design of the package is also available for display in your game. The rest of the patch notes are entirely about various bug fixes, so not much more there. You can see the full change log on Nintendo’s support website.

#3963. Metro 2039 goes back to its Metro underground roots, with a story shaped by the war in Ukraine and the people who suffer it

Metro 2039 takes us back to the tunnels of the Moscow Metro where, fittingly, Nazi ideology never died.

The Metro series is finally, officially back with a new installment. 4A Games has just unveiled Metro 2039 to the world, the follow-up to the outstanding Metro Exodus, released all the way back in 2019.

2039 takes an unusual route with its scope, however. Rather than build on the semi-open-world structure of Exodus, the upcoming sequel instead brings the focus back to where it all began: the Metro.

What won’t be changing is the kind of game that it is. Metro 2039 remains, like its predecessors, a story-driven, single-player game. Returning to the confined spaces of the Moscow Metro brings the focus back to the claustrophobic, uneasy atmosphere of the original games.

The game’s protagonist is, for the first time, going to be voiced throughout. From what we’ve been able to see, the psychological horror in this installment will be driven more by the very real effects the apocalypse has had, and continues to have, on denizens of the Metro.

2039 has been in development for years, but 4A Games has been rocked by two considerable events: the 2020 Covid pandemic, and Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine, where the developer is based. The game’s darker story has changed in response to that.

The team’s Ukrainian perspective is molded into the narrative, and more prominently represents the toll the events of the last several years has taken on members of the team, their families and communities.

According to the developer, you can expect a bigger emphasis on choice and consequence, with Russian author Dmitry Glukhovsky returning to co-write a narrative that explores the compromised morality of a post-war society.

The new protagonist’s return to the Metro comes with the reveal that the different underground factions are now united under one banner, the not-so-subtly named Novoreich. Lead by a former Spartan, the Novoreich is an authoritarian regime which offers what it believes to be the only path to salvation.

4A Games remains majority Ukrainian, with teams based in Kyiv, and Malta. Unlike most AAA projects today, the studio continues to rely on its own engine tech. The 4A Engine is given a major upgrade for 2039: ray tracing is now a core component of the rendering pipeline, but the tech has been rebuilt to run better on modern hardware.

Today’s reveal sadly didn’t feature much gameplay - only a brief first-look with a mix of gameplay and cinematics. The developer, however, emphasised that creating cluttered, believable and lived-in environments remains a key focus.

Metro 2039 is set for release sometime this winter on PC, Xbox Series X/S, and PS5.

#3960. Blizzard will talk about Diablo 4: Lord of Hatred one last time before the expansion's launch next week

We're well under two weeks from the launch of Diablo 4's next expansion, Lord of Hatred, but there's more yet to be said.

Diablo 4 is mere days away from the launch of its biggest expansion yet, and Blizzard wants to make sure it got one last chance to tell you about it. Lord of Hatred is the follow-up to 2024’s Vessel of Hatred, and it’s set to arrive on April 28.

Next week, however, we’re getting an updated look at the new content as part of a livestream. This is the Developer Update kind; the meaty, information-dense show anyone who follows Diablo’s livestreams should be familiar with.

The next Developer Update is set for Thursday, April 23. It’ll kick off at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 6pm GMT. The show will, naturally, focus on Lord of Hatred. In particular, we’re getting another look at the expansion content that hasn’t been given the same level of coverage as the bigger features.

Everyone knows about the new Skovos region, the Warlock class (and the Paladin before that), but we haven’t seen much from the other gameplay-altering features that affect a lot of the core flow.

In next week’s showcase, Blizzard will show off the updated and expanded skill trees - which come to all classes, the Talisman system, and the gear-altering Horadric Cube. War Plans, the new make-your-own-endgame feature will be discussed, too.

More interestingly, we’re also going to hear about the new season kicking off right alongside the launch of Lord of Hatred. A short, in-betweener season is currently live in Diablo 4, and it’s going to end right as the next one/the expansion launch.

And, of course, the show won’t end before the team takes a few questions from chat, as is tradition. If you want to catch it live, you’ll be able to do so on Diablo’s official YouTube, Twitch, Twitter, and TikTok channels.

#3958. The Sims 4's much maligned paid mods have made it to consoles, but Kits are coming back to PC

The Sims 4's Marketplace and user-created content have officially arrived on consoles, a little over a month after their debut on PC.

The Sims 4 players on PlayStation and Xbox have now caught up to their friends on PC, at least when it comes to the game’s Marketplace. This new feature is essentially a hub for paid mods and other user-created content.

As often happens when long-established games introduce paid mods, The Sims 4’s wasn’t especially well-received, in part because of the introduction of a new premium currency - Moola - that is the only way to purchase any of that content.

The Moola denominations and prices are similar to many other in-game currencies, and the criticism around them is the same: they obfuscate the true value of items, and because of the way those denominations are structured, you’ll never be able to buy exactly what you need.

For most games, the subject of paid mods has always been fraught, and that's certainly true for The Sims 4. In the announcement blog post, Maxis said that the launch on consoles will work similarly to what PC players have seen, in that Kits will no longer be available to buy directly with real money on the PlayStation and Microsoft Stores. While Expansion Packs, Game Packs, and Stuff Packs will remain, you’ll need to buy Moola if you want to acquire Kits going forward.

Interestingly, however, EA seems to have changed its mind somewhat on the Kits situation. A recently leaked memo (via SimsCommunity), appears to show that the publisher intends on making Kits available for purchase directly again, without the need for Moola.

Unfortunately, this only appears to affect the PC version, with the reversion reportedly forthcoming on both the EA App as well as Steam. Indeed, according to the same report, the change has already taken place on the former, with the latter following on April 20.

Considering the Marketplace only just launched on consoles, the company may wait to see if the decision to remove Kits from console platform marketplaces will be as poorly received as it has been on PC.

If you’re looking to jump back into The Sims 4 to check out all the new paid content, make sure you’re well-equipped with our list of Sims 4 cheats and debug options, or this one specifically for the Royalty & Legacy expansion cheats.

#3957. Crusader Kings publishers Paradox announce CEO swap, say they're "in a strong position at a time when much of the industry is facing major challenges"

"My plan was never to be CEO for life", says man clearly not embracing the grand strategy despot spirit

Paradox Interactive, publishers of umpteen strategy genre stalwarts including Crusader Kings, Europa Universalis, and Hearts of Iron, have announced plans to switch overlords early next year. Fredrik Wester will make way for Mattias Lilja, as the deputy CEO takes the throne.

While the move's been announced this week, Lilja will properly become boss from January 4th, making this a case of getting a new figurehead in place as the calendars swap. Departing CEO Fredrik Wester isn't going far, at least for now, as he'll "continue focusing on the company's long-term development as a member of the board".

"My plan was never to be CEO for life," Wester said. "The goal was to build the foundation before passing the baton on for the next chapter in the company’s journey. Since I returned as CEO, we’ve streamlined our strategy, rebuilt our pipeline and developed our commercial offering. Mattias has had a central role in laying this foundation, and now is the right time to hand over."

"The Board wants to thank Fredrik for his visionary leadership and outstanding contributions over these years," stated chairman Håkan Sjunnesson. "As a result, Paradox is in a strong position at a time when much of the industry is facing major challenges." He added that Lilja is "more than ready to assume the role and lead Paradox towards new gaming experiences that last for decades".

Lilja himself declared that Paradox have "a unique DNA that has made us one of the greats in deep and engaging strategy and management games" and will be "stepping up the pace". "We will make further investments in our core business, push the boundaries of our game design, work even more closely with our loyal players, develop more and better tools and services that benefit both modders and players, and continue to sharpen our ways of working and our organisation, with player value in focus," he said.

As Wester alluded to, he previously served as Paradox CEO from 2009 to 2018, with a brief stint as executive chairman of the board sandwiched between that and his latest stint as CEO since 2021. Lilja has been deputy CEO since 2024 and chief of staff since 2021, having originally joined Paradox as a producer in 2009.

The past half decade has been a very mixed bag for Paradox. Their big strategy flagships keep ticking along, albeit with the question of whether their next DLC will feel worth it hovering overhead near-permanently. Outside of that, however, the likes of Cities: Skylines 2, Vampire: The Masquerade Bloodlines 2, and cancelled Sims competitor Life By You have made for a track record heavy on questionable decisions and games which either flopped hard or failed to blow away expectations. Wester acknowledged back in 2024 that the company had "made the wrong calls in several projects, especially outside of our core".

With the likes of post-apocalyptic strategy game Afterworld currently in the works, it'll be interesting to see if Lilja's tenure can see Paradox finally start to nail not just their nerdy bread and butter, but also games that don't involve staring down at a big map.

#3956. Naval warfare, an actual server browser and more on the way to Battlefield 6 this year as BF Studios reveals 2026 roadmap

2026 is looking very exciting for Battlefield 6, even if much of what's coming is based on things we already know, and some we've long been asking for.

It took Battlefield Studios over four months to tell Battlefield 6 players what they can actually expect from the game over the course of this year, in terms of content - but we’re glad to see a plan laid out nonetheless.

The developer unveiled a grand 2026 roadmap, covering three more seasons currently in the works, and a wealth of new additions across the entire game, including new maps and the introduction of a new theatre of combat.

In a wide-ranging new video dubbed The Year Ahead, members of the Battlefield 6 development team have revealed a lot of new information about the future of the multiplayer shooter, going over plenty of the features and new content coming over the course of this year.

The video confirmed that BF6 has at least three other seasons in the works. Season 3, which begins in May, will be followed by Season 4, and Season 5 later in the year. Season 5 is the most mysterious, which is understandable.

We’ve known about some of what’s coming in Season 3, such as the remake of Golmud Railway (now called Railway to Golmud), but the video also revealed that a remake of Battlefield 3’s Grand Bazaar - now Cairo Bazaar - will also arrive later in the same season. Other exciting additions, such as battle royale solos and ranked play for Redsec are also on the agenda for Season 3.

Season 4, set for July, looks to be the biggest so far, with the introduction of naval combat, which will be available across two maps. Tsuru Reef, which is said to be even larger than Golmud, the largest map in BF6. The Pacific-set map won’t be the only one, as later in the season, another remake will arrive, this time of the iconic Wake Island.

The introduction of naval combat will bring with it a new dynamic wave system, aircraft carriers with operational flight decks, and new naval vehicles. Custom lobbies and Spectator Mode are also planned for Season 4.

Season 5 will bring three maps to BF6, rather than two, but all of its content remains under wraps.

Perhaps a sour note is that almost all of the maps referenced and shown in the video are remakes of maps from other Battlefield games, or reimagined at the very least. The Battlefield series is no stranger to remaking its own maps, but Battlefield 6 appears to be leaning on it much more than past entries.

If it’s any consolation, however, the map remakes we’ve played so far in Battlefield 6 have gone through major changes that have contributed to giving them a different flow and feel from their classic versions, or even remakes in other BF games.

Over the course of 2026, you can also expect the return of persistent servers, as well as a server browser to find them all - just like the good ol’ days. This includes the ability to host your own, though it’s unclear quite how this is going to work.

Season 3 is set to revealed in the coming days, so you’ll be hearing back from BF Studios in the near future.

#3955. Worst Class Ever takes asymmetrical multiplayer back to school, with a teacher player trying to spot the naughty children among the NPCs

Master the sinful art of eating sweets behind your textbook

What's the best prank you ever pulled on a teacher in school, assuming you went to school? By which I mean, a genuinely funny prank that didn't cause any injuries, break any of the more important laws (legal or ethical), or leave anybody with years of mental distress.

I'll start: I once had to write a four-page punishment essay with the topic "silence is golden", after being caught talking in class. I took the essay very seriously for the first three pages, only to end it with the phrase "...but not as golden as my arse." The teacher who set me the essay smugly tore it up without reading it - as I knew he would. Checkmate, Mr Thompson. Decades later, the last laugh remains mine.

Worst Class Ever is a new don't-call-it-friendslop asymmetrical multiplayer game dedicated to such larks. One player is a teacher, and seven others are naughty delinquent children, hiding in amongst some well-brought-up and obedient NPCs. As the wayward tykes, your goal is to do mischievous things like eating at your desk, passing notes, dropping banana skins, and playing on your phone, without being spotted by Teach.

All of this takes place in a breezy modern Japanese high school, the kind familiar from a million animes. Bagsy the Protagonist Desk by the window at the back of the class! The maplist spans the curriculum, from computer labs to gym tracks to stepped lecture theatres. I don't think there are any covert edu-tainment mechanics, but if you're playing Teacher, I guess there's nothing to stop you actually explaining the periodic table while trying to work out who keeps throwing chalk at your head.

What a wholesome and whimsical place! Such happy memories! Oh crikey, the male teacher is terrifying – why can't he stop grinning? And why do I have a smoke grenade? Why is this lesson taking place in the dark? Why are the teachers permitted to punch the students and tie them to wooden posts? Worst Class Ever definitely isn't a horror game, but I'm not sure I'd send my kids to this particular institution. I feel like we're one texture pack away from playing a more sociable version of Little Nightmares. Read more on Steam.

Xbox is bagging up former PlayStation exclusives like crazy, with Nioh 3 Complete Edition making its way to Xbox Series X|S on January 28, 2027.

Nioh follows Helldivers 2, the Final Fantasy VII Remake trilogy and PHYSINT by hopping aboard Xbox hardware. It's lovely to see renowned franchises like the dark samurai souls-like Nioh arrive on Xbox. It certainly beats seeing Halo and Gears launch on PS5 without anything major coming the other way.

Nioh 3 Complete Edition is an action RPG, in which players don the role of shogun Takechiyo, facing off against punishing soulslike scraps and challenges. Team NINJA shared a press release confirming the game is headed to Nintendo Switch 2 and Xbox on January 28, 2027, complete with Xbox Play Anywhere support.

Nioh 3's second DLC, Bloody Insurrection, is set for December 17, 2026 for PS5 and Steam. The DLC will be included in the Complete Edition when it arrives early next year. As a franchise, Nioh has consistently wooed players with it's punishing combat and flashy action, with the third game holding an 86 on Metacritic.

Exciting times, eh? I wonder if this means Xbox players might gain access to Nioh 1 or 2 ports at some point in the future. Personally, I've always heard good things about the Nioh games, so it would be great to experience the entire series on Xbox, should Koei Tecmo make them available.

#3953. GTA 6 Performs Better on Xbox Series X Than Base PS5, Despite All of Sony's Marketing

Even though Sony has paid god-only-knows how much money to market GTA 6 as a borderline PS5 exclusive, it turns out that Rockstar's magnum opus actually runs better on Xbox.

This is according to those tech wizards over at Digital Foundry, who have spent hours comparing the open world title across base PS5, PS5 Pro, Xbox Series X, and Xbox Series S.

Now, we already know that GTA 6 isn't perfect on the standard PS5. It suffers from minor but sometimes prolonged frame rate drops during busy scenes — whether you're speeding through heavy traffic or fighting for your life in a particularly explosive combat encounter.

But in a rather shocking twist, the Xbox Series X outdoes the PS5 in this department. While Digital Foundry's testing shows that the frame rate dips are still present on the Series X, they're nowhere near as frequent.

They write: "PS5 suffers substantially more frequent frame rate drops than Series X, which is compounded by the fact that the Xbox machine also benefits from 120Hz VRR support to smooth out minor dips."

The article continues: "Ultimately, Series X is meaningfully better off."

This isn't what you'd expect, given that every PlayStation-related GTA 6 advertisement and trailer has boasted that the game 'Plays Best on PS5'.

Okay, so that slogan might technically be true if we're counting the PS5 Pro, where GTA 6 does perform best by some distance, thanks to a combination of the console's PSSR upscaler and increased GPU power.

But on base hardware, it's Microsoft that wins out.

"Overall, the PS5 Pro leads the rankings with its superior visual detail and rock-solid 30fps target, followed by the Xbox Series X — which edges out the standard PS5 through better performance stability," Digital Foundry concludes.

Are you surprised by these findings? Have you noticed any frequent frame rate drops in GTA 6 on PS5? Wonder if we'll ever see 60fps again in the comments section below.

#3952. Lords Of The Fallen 2 Launches April 2027, Final Date Coming Next Month

Publisher CI Games has announced that Lords of the Fallen 2 will launch in April 2027.

This comes via a social media post from founder and CEO Marek Tyminski (thanks, Gematsu), who simply said "Lords of the Fallen II: April 2027. Exact date in December". So yes, we'll keep an eye out for a further update and let you know when exactly you can expect the game to drop.

The game was previously delayed into 'Q1 2027' earlier this year, with Tyminski explaining that the stacked 2026 schedule – which includes Zelda: Ocarina of Time and a little game called GTA 6 – led to a desire to give Lords of the Fallen 2 a bit of space to shine.

"This updated release window also strategically positions Lords of the Fallen II outside of a highly competitive holiday period, ensuring the game receives the dedicated attention it deserves."

It's honestly not a bad choice at all, and we're thankful to see at least one game escape the avalanche of releases in 2026. Hell, we've still got a bunch of big-hitters coming in December, including Rayman Legends Retold, Monster Hunter Wilds, Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World, and Professor Layton and The New World of Steam.

Guide Our Most Anticipated Nintendo Switch 1 & 2 Games In 2026

#3951. While soulslikes went bigger than big, Death's Door swung open the appeal of a tighter adventure

Declaring a Best Way of Doing Things is a fool’s game, though in recent years my favourite entries in the Tricky Hitting genre – inclusive of soulslikes and their hybridised disciples – have been the big, bulging ones. Elden Rings and Silksongs, with vast kingdoms and deep, rattling toolkits for surviving them. The reason it’s a fool’s game is because you can also have something like Death’s Door, a taut, compact, lighthearted little actioner that fills eight hours instead of 80 and yet never feels underwhelming or compromised for it.

Have You Played? is an endless stream of game retrospectives.

Even in the latter stages, with a full kit of precisely four ranged spells, Death’s Door is a simple proposition. You are a crow. You hit things. Occasionally you shoot things. You collect the souls of a frog, a yeti, and a grandmother. Everything in-between directly relates to finding the errant monster/pensioner, or at a stretch, upgrading one of those four abilities.

Still, it’s clever with its limitations. Environments are small in number but vary wildly in tone and texture, and they tightly weave their paths into criss-crossing bundles that maximise travel – evoking the sense of a great, ranging adventure within relatively tiny spaces. The lack of a wiki’s worth of combat options also never becomes a problem, partly because it spreads out its spell unlocks, and partly because the smooth, flowing back-and-forths of its central swordplay are pleasurable enough to carry it anyway. Good bosses, too! They’re all characterful, memorable weirdoes who fight unlike anyone in their minion armies, and usually come with a hidden weakness to deduce and exploit.

Which is welcome, as these big lads and lasses do tend to launch difficulty spikes right up your feathered backside, and do so in a game that isn’t otherwise as fussed about trial-and-error pain endurance as some of its inspirations. They don’t, however, bring the mood down. At times, this tale of a pitch-black soul reaper working as an agent of Death (complete with an office of Death and embittered co-workers of Death) can get downright cosy, leading through you through warmly-lit jungles and breezy waterside ruins.

Recently replaying, I’d also forgotten how witty it can be. Little gaglets are sprinkled throughout, both visual and verbal, but the best jokes are saved for – funnily enough – the bosses, who’ll raise your pre-fight spirit with some amusingly terrible trash talk before becoming the punchline themselves. I audibly wheezed the first time a death animation immediately cut to the foe’s impromptu funeral, their beaked killer among the precious few guests. And even when the joke is recycled later, I couldn’t help tittering at the sight of my enemy – who seconds earlier, had been attempting to fatally sit on me – lying nobly in state.

I previously considered ending my Valor Mortis review by calling it a gateway into the more demanding side of action-RPGs; a shorter, simpler alternative to FromSoft’s overwhelming titans that might nonetheless serve to introduce curious newcomers to their shared quirks and qualities. The game equivalent of splashing your chest with water before jumping into a pool. In hindsight, Death’s Door was always a better fit for that description, though there’s enough else here you don’t need to be prepping for something tougher to appreciate its lean, keen adventuring.
